import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    corr_threshold = 0.6
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    keep = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(ids):
        is_duplicate = False
        for j in range(i):
            if ids[j] in keep:
                corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.x[:, j])[0, 1]
                if abs(corr) >= corr_threshold:
                    is_duplicate = True
                    break
        if not is_duplicate:
            keep.append(fid)
    
    # Select top features by t-statistic
    t_stats = []
    for fid in keep:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, col_idx]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, col_idx]
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)
        t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
    
    # Sort by t-statistic and select top candidates
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1][:len(keep)]
    selected_ids = [keep[i] for i in sorted_indices[:20]]
    
    # Use mutual information to select final features
    mi_scores = mutual_info_classif(feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_ids]], feats.y)
    final_indices = np.argsort(mi_scores)[::-1][:10]
    final_ids = [selected_ids[i] for i in final_indices]
    
    # Build logistic regression with L1 penalty to identify drivers
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in final_ids]])
    
    # Fit logistic regression with L1 regularization
    lr = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', random_state=42)
    lr.fit(X_scaled, feats.y)
    
    # Get coefficients and identify important features
    coef = lr.coef_[0]
    significant_indices = np.where(np.abs(coef) > 1e-5)[0]
    
    if len(significant_indices) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select top drivers by coefficient magnitude
    driver_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(coef[significant_indices]))[::-1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
    drivers = tuple([final_ids[significant_indices[i]] for i in driver_indices])
    
    # Build columns and products
    columns = tuple(final_ids)
    products = ()
    
    # Build loadings
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(final_ids):
        loadings[fid] = coef[i]
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
